correctness.rationale: Both graph constructors satisfy the strongly regular relation \(A^2=4I+2\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\). Explicit spectral projectors yield the necessary/sufficient dark-subspace formula \(D_T=15-\operatorname{rank}B_T-\operatorname{rank}C_T\) for each nine-site subset. Strict positivity of losses proves all no-jump eigenvalues have strictly negative imaginary parts if and only if D_T=0. All 11,440 masks per graph were enumerated exactly by a fraction-free rank checker, independently matched by a two-prime Krylov checker with rigorous Hadamard minor bounds. Complete count and positive-loss quantifiers are proved; no sampling-to-infinity inference is made.

value.rationale: The least feasible detector number is forced by a natural ninefold eigenvalue degeneracy, making the complete exact minimal-placement census a motivated invariant rather than an arbitrary selected subset size. Two indistinguishable-at-spectrum strongly regular quantum networks have sharply different fractions of fully capturing nine-site placements (3,936/11,440 versus 7,200/11,440), plus different complete dark-space distributions. The invariant can guide coherent detector-placement robustness and distinguishes global placement distributions while acknowledging local induced-pattern equivalence.
